Alright. Let me pull something useful from what we haven't touched yet. There's a section on conditional routing — where the graph isn't fixed at design time. A router node inspects a result and decides which path fires next. Like, classify a support ticket, then branch to the right handler. Or check a diff size, then either do a quick review or spin up a full audit. The clever part: the router's *decision* can be model-powered, but the *routing itself* is code the model wrote. So you get Claude's judgment at the decision point, but script reliability at the execution — no surprise "Claude decided to skip the audit" moments.
